I haven't sent anything. Your other wallet looks compromised, and the 0.5 ETH would be taken as soon as it arrived.

**What I found:**
- 0x6bd36310cec97dcb2499fafe285b48a6f8d0fd13 isn't a plain wallet. It carries an EIP-7702 delegation to a contract at 0x143b41298cb0a6a83b3ab532aaafbbae3078bc46.
- I checked that contract's code. Whenever the wallet receives ETH, the code automatically forwards the wallet's entire ETH balance to a hardcoded address, **0x99999ff41e99629aef404025e66db546e3e99999**.
- The same contract can also move out all of the wallet's ERC-20 tokens, NFTs and ERC-1155 tokens, and only 0x9999…9999 can call those functions. This matches the "sweeper" contracts attackers install after they get hold of a wallet's private key.

**What this means:**
- Any ETH you send there for gas would go straight to 0x9999…9999. Your 1 ETH balance here is safe because nothing was sent.
- If you didn't set up this delegation yourself, assume the private key or seed phrase for 0x6bd3…fd13 has been exposed.

**What I'd suggest:**
1. Stop sending funds to 0x6bd3…fd13.
2. Move any assets still in that wallet out through a recovery service that bundles the gas payment and the transfer into one private transaction, such as Flashbots bundles. Sending gas there the normal way won't work.
3. Make a new wallet with a new seed phrase, and check whether the same seed controls any of your other accounts, including this one.
